🌍 Pezeshkian condoles passing of renowned novelist and traveloguer, Reza Amirkhani

📌 Tehran, IRNA — President Masoud Pezeshkian has extended his condolences over the passing of Reza Amirkhani, a well-known writer, novelist, travelogue writer, and literary critic, saying he will be remembered for opening a new horizon in contemporary fiction writing.

In a condolence message on Monday, Pezeshkian admired the career of late Amirkhani, calling him an author who have had a profound perspective on humanity and society, a creative command over language, and possessing a unique narrative style.
​
Pointing to some of his works such as “Dastan-e Sistan”, “Ermia”, “Man-e Ou”, “Bi-Vatan” and “Gheydar”, the President said they not merely recount events or portray characters, rather provide a framework for reflecting on concepts such as faith, love, identity, chivalry, responsibility, and social belonging.
​
He said that although Amirkhani’s death a significant loss for the nation’s cultural and literary community, but his name and works will endure in the history of contemporary literature, and future generations will continue to benefit from his legacy.
​
Pezeshkian concluded his message by extending his condolences to the family, the community of writers, the realm of culture and literature, while praying mercy and forgiveness to the deceased, and patience and well-being to the bereaved.
​
Amirkhani died at the age of 54 after suffering complications from a paragliding accident for nearly a year. He authored numerous works, including novels, travelogues, short stories, and social and cultural essays.
